name: Bags
author: brodgar
description: Example addon (032-replace-verb): hafen.ui.on(selector, 'appear') + widget:replace(view) — replace the native inventory with a custom read-only view that draws the REAL items at their real grid positions ('wrap, don't reimplement', D-009). Two ordinary pieces of API and nothing in between: `on` WAITS for the part of the UI you name with a selector — inventory[title=Inventory], the one that resolves to the main inventory and nothing else (032.1) — and fires for what is ALREADY open (D-068), while `replace` is a VERB ON THE WIDGET that puts your own window in place of the client's. hafen.ui.replace(type, opts, fn) and its server descriptor {id,type,place,caption,parentType} are a HARD CUT (032.2, D-012): a second vocabulary for 'which window', and the only thing that could bind a view to a hidden native window. THE TRAP THE VERB OWNS: it hides the ENCLOSING WINDOW, not the widget you point at, so replacing the inventory GRID takes the whole stock window rather than leaving its frame around a hole (widget:hide() still hides exactly what you point at — that is the difference). DORMANT until you press the 'toggle' hotkey (unbound until you assign it under Options > Keybindings > Bags; suggested Ctrl+Shift+I), which ARMS and DISARMS the replacement; arming while your inventory is already open replaces it on the spot. Item moving (take/transfer/drop) is the gated Phase-4 actions tier, so the view is read-only (a click logs the item). 031: THE CLIENT'S OWN TOGGLE COMES WITH THE WINDOW — hiding a native window makes it yours, toggle included, and the view you pass to :replace is what that toggle drives, so once replaced TAB and the inventory menu button open and close the custom 'Bags' window and the menu tick reads that window's own visibility (before this, Tab flipped `visible` back on the very window bags had hidden and the stock inventory came back ON TOP of the custom one). The hotkey is therefore an ARM/DISARM switch, not a show/hide key — that is Tab's job now — and disarming (or the view's X, or disable/:reload) gives the window and its key back under ONE rule: the stock inventory ends up AS THE USER WAS SEEING IT, open if the custom view was on screen and closed if it was not.
